html:
The first independent trade union in the Soviet bloc, founded in Poland in September 1980. It grew into a mass movement that ended communist rule in Poland in 1989.

In August 1980 workers at the Lenin Shipyard in Gdańsk went on strike after the firing of a crane operator, Anna Walentynowicz. Strikes spread along the coast, led by an electrician, Lech Wałęsa. The government gave way and allowed a free union. Within a year about ten million people, a third of the working age population, had joined. The election of the Polish Pope John Paul II in 1978 had given Poles new confidence.

In December 1981 General Wojciech Jaruzelski declared martial law, banned Solidarity and jailed its leaders. It survived underground, and Wałęsa won the Nobel Peace Prize in 1983.

By 1989 the economy was failing, and Gorbachev would not send Soviet troops. Round Table talks led to partly free elections in June 1989, which Solidarity swept. A Solidarity led government took office, and the revolutions of 1989 followed.
sum: The first independent trade union in the Soviet bloc, founded in Poland in September 1980. It grew into a mass movement that ended communist rule in Poland in 1989.
